\begin{theorem}[Characterization of algebraic degree bounds]
\lean{FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff}
\label{FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.anfSupport}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb N$, and let $c$ assign a coefficient in the field with two elements
to every subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Its algebraic degree is at most $r$ if and only if
every subset with nonzero coefficient has cardinality at most $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of ANF coefficients]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_add}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_add, FABL.anfEval_anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_injective}
\difficulty{3}
For any two functions $f,g:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$, the coefficient function of
their pointwise sum is the pointwise sum of their coefficient functions: for every
subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $\widehat{f+g}(S)=\widehat f(S)+\widehat g(S)$ in
$\mathbb F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficients of the zero function]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_zero}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_injective}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean function $f$ on $
\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the coefficients of its algebraic normal form are all zero when $f$ is
the zero function.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of the zero coefficient function]
\lean{FABL.algebraicDegree_zero}
\label{FABL.algebraicDegree_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.anfSupport}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$. The coefficient function that assigns zero to every subset of
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$ has algebraic degree zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of the zero function]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_zero}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.algebraicDegree_zero, FABL.anfCoeff_zero, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, the zero function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean
cube over $\mathbb{F}_2$ to $\mathbb{F}_2$ has algebraic degree $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a sum of ANF coefficients]
\lean{FABL.algebraicDegree_add_le_max}
\label{FABL.algebraicDegree_add_le_max}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $c,d$ assign an element of the field with two elements to
each subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The algebraic degree of their pointwise sum, computed
in that field, is at most the maximum of their algebraic degrees:
\[
\deg(c+d)\le\max\{\deg(c),\deg(d)\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a sum of Boolean functions]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_add_le_max}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_add_le_max}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.algebraicDegree_add_le_max, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfCoeff_add, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree}
\difficulty{3}
For any two Boolean functions on the $n$-dimensional cube over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the
algebraic degree of their pointwise sum over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is at most the maximum of
their algebraic degrees.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for ANF multiplication]
\lean{FABL.algebraicDegree_anfMul_le_add}
\label{FABL.algebraicDegree_anfMul_le_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ANFCoefficients, FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff, FABL.anfMul}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $c,d$ assign coefficients in the field with two elements to
every subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Define their product by assigning to each subset $U$
the coefficient $\sum_{S,T:\,S\cup T=U}c(S)d(T)$, with the sum taken in the field with
two elements. Then the algebraic degree of this product is at most the sum of the
algebraic degrees of $c$ and $d$:
\[
\deg(cd)\le\deg(c)+\deg(d).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficients of a product]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_mul}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_anfMul, FABL.anfEval_injective, FABL.anfMul}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb F_2$. For every coordinate
subset $U$, the algebraic normal form coefficient of the pointwise product $fg$ at $U$
equals the sum, over all pairs of coordinate subsets $S,T$ with $S\cup T=U$, of the
product of the coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and the coefficient of $g$ at $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Algebraic degree of a product]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_mul_le_add}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_mul_le_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.algebraicDegree_anfMul_le_add, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfCoeff_mul, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and all functions
$f,g:(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n\to\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, the algebraic degree of their
pointwise product is at most the sum of their algebraic degrees. Here the algebraic
degree is the largest cardinality of a set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose coefficient
in the algebraic normal form is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of the Constant-One Function]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_one}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_one}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, the constant-one function on the $n$-dimensional
Boolean cube over the field with two elements has algebraic degree $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[ANF coefficients of a monomial]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_anfMonomial}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff_anfMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval, FABL.anfEval_anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval_injective, FABL.anfMonomial}
\difficulty{3}
For every set of coordinates $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the coefficient function of the
monomial $x\mapsto\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ is $1$ at $S$ and $0$ at every other set of
coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a Boolean monomial]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_anfMonomial}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_anfMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.anfCoeff_anfMonomial, FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.anfSupport, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree}
\difficulty{4}
For every subset $S$ of the $n$ coordinate indices, the Boolean function
$x\mapsto\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ has algebraic degree equal to $|S|$, with the product taken
in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a Boolean monomial]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_anfMonomial_le_card}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_anfMonomial_le_card}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_anfMonomial}
\difficulty{1}
For a natural number $n$ and a subset $S$ of the coordinate set $	ext{Fin}(n)$, the
function on the Boolean cube over $br/	ext{?}$ given by the product of the coordinates
indexed by $S$ has algebraic degree at most $|S|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a finite product]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_finset_prod_le}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_finset_prod_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_mul_le_add, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $\iota$ be any type, let $s$ be a finite set of indices in $\iota$,
and for each $i\in\iota$ let $g_i:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$. The algebraic degree
of the pointwise product of the functions indexed by $s$ is at most the sum of their
algebraic degrees.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for finite sums]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_finset_sum_le}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_finset_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_add_le_max}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $r$ be nonnegative integers, let $s$ be a finite set of indices, and let
$g_i$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional binary cube to the two-element field for
each index $i$. If every $g_i$ with $i\in s$ has algebraic degree at most $r$, then the
pointwise sum of the functions indexed by $s$, with values in the two-element field, has
algebraic degree at most $r$.
\end{theorem}
